structured_review.summary: Slice 020B.1 delivers all five dispatch-package ACs structurally: fixture-pass/ and fixture-fail/ trees are present with schema-valid expected-annotations.json files, conftest.md and WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md exist, workflow-selftest.yml is syntactically valid YAML, and schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json is correctly included as a fourth trigger path. The normalize() comparison correctly strips variable fields (pr_sha, base_ref, workflow_run_id). The artifact stash-and-delete pattern correctly handles the naming collision between two sequential policy-check-summary uploads. D-021 is not used in any deliverable; STATUS.md/DECISIONS.md/BACKLOG.md are excluded from scope_boundary and appear unmodified; 020D1's assumption that workflow-selftest.yml exists is satisfied. One CRIT blocks approval: the selftest invokes policy-check.yml twice with an identical PR context (same SCP_BASE_SHA / SCP_HEAD_SHA), producing identical outputs both times. When 020C updates fixture-fail/services.yml to carry a deliberate rule violation, that file appears in changed-files.txt for both invocations, both produce deny findings, and the comparison of the first invocation's output against fixture-pass/expected-annotations.json (which expects empty findings) will fail — permanently breaking the selftest at the 020C boundary. WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md documents the transition intention but not the isolation gap or a viable mechanism. Two MAJs also block: the hardcoded SHA @9928ecc has no documented maintenance procedure for future policy-check.yml edits, and plan §4 020B.1's trigger-path list omits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json, creating a plan-vs-implementation discrepancy in the governance canonical.
